lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 8, Session 2
lesson.footer: Persuasive Speeches | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 8 Session 2

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 planning spoken persuasive texts with evidence; VC2E5LY08 selecting information to support a point of view; VC2E5LA03 language to persuade
plan.shape: model, guide, apply: the teacher gathers and ranks proof for the shade-trees speech, students sort evidence types and rank arguments, then gather proof for their own speech
plan.criticalFeature: the order of arguments builds the audience's feeling: strong, stronger, strongest last
decisionPoints: the What kind of proof? round
the choice check: the order that builds best
the exit board: rank three reasons for a new speech
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: Prove it, and save the best for last.
plan.catchUp: Students without an S1 plan use the planner frame on the Supported Worksheet.

studentTools: S1 speech plan (in the speech folder)
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Three kinds of proof: 1 fact or number, 2 expert, 3 example or story

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: sort the proof, pick the stronger proof, rank the arguments, then gather proof for your own speech.

example.prompt: Shade cuts UV by up to 75% (Cancer Council).
example.answer: A fact or number, from an expert group.

items.prompt: Sort the proof: FACT, EXPERT or STORY.
cards: Our yard hit 41 degrees in February.
A doctor says sunburn can lead to cancer.
Mia fainted after soccer in the sun.
Trees can cool a street by several degrees.
Our principal says hot kids learn less.
Last summer, nobody could use the slide.

FACT: Our yard hit 41 degrees in February.
Trees can cool a street by several degrees.
EXPERT: A doctor says sunburn can lead to cancer.
Our principal says hot kids learn less.
STORY: Mia fainted after soccer in the sun.
Last summer, nobody could use the slide.

items.hint: Who said it? What happened? Is there a number?

example.prompt: Claim: we need a crossing guard.
example.answer: Twelve near misses this term beats lots of cars go past.

options: Turtles mistake plastic bags for jellyfish.
Doctors say kids need 9 to 11 hours.

items.prompt: Claim: our library needs more books.
options: We have one book on space for 400 kids.

example.answer: Birds like trees, then cooler play, then skin cancer.

items.prompt: Write the letters in order so the strongest comes last.
rows: A: it's fun with friends. B: fewer cars keeps us safe. C: saves petrol.
A: ads are annoying. B: kids copy what they see. C: diabetes is rising in kids.
A: bears are cute. B: sea ice is shrinking. C: cubs are starving.
answers: A: it's fun with friends. B: fewer cars keeps us safe. C: saves petrol.
A: ads are annoying. B: kids copy what they see. C: diabetes is rising in kids.
A: bears are cute. B: sea ice is shrinking. C: cubs are starving.
A, B, C (accept B last with a reason)

example.answer: 1 Birds: trees bring wildlife. 2 Cooler: yard hit 41 degrees. 3 Safer: shade cuts UV by up to 75%.

the company wants to sell it

items.answer: A small, specific story that links back to the argument.

items.prompt: A doctor says sunburn is dangerous.
Write the reasons in order: weak, stronger, strongest.
items.hint: Reasons for plastic: it kills sea animals, it looks messy, it fills the tip.

example.answer: My best reason is shade stops sunburn. I know because shade cuts UV by 75%.

items.prompt: My best reason is ___. I know because ___.
items.answer: A reason and one piece of proof.
items.hint: Use your plan from last session.

slides.notes: Open S2. One line: a claim without proof is just an opinion.
Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Students need their S1 plan from the speech folder.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to choose proof and order arguments so a speech builds.
successCriteria: I can tell a fact, an expert and a story apart.
I can order three arguments so the strongest comes last.
I can test whether proof can be trusted.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday you chose your side. Today you prove it.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Which would make you believe it?
lines: Claim: our yard is too hot.
1: It's really hot. 2: It hit 41 degrees. 3: Mia fainted at soccer.

notes.answer: 2 or 3 - exact proof beats it's really hot
beats: SAY: One claim, three ways to prove it.
ASK: Which proof convinces you most? 1, 2 or 3?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2 or 3
ASK: Why is 1 the weakest?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: it's just an opinion; no proof
SAY: Numbers and stories both work. Saying really doesn't.
trap: thinking a louder claim is proof.
Fix: ask how would we check that?

slides.meaning: To put things in order, from least to most.
slides.example: Rank your reasons: save the strongest for last.

notes.answer: to put things in order, from least to most
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Rank. Say it with me. Rank.
SAY: To put things in order, from least to most.
SAY: Rank your reasons: save the strongest for last.
ASK: Why save the strongest reason for last?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: it's what they remember; it builds up
trap: thinking rank means remove the weak ones.
Fix: say we keep all three, we just order them.

slides.title: Proof for my shade trees speech

rows: Story: the magpies left when the old gum came down.
Fact: our yard hit 41 degrees in February.
Expert: Cancer Council says shade cuts UV by up to 75%.

notes.answer: birds, then cooler play, then skin protection last
beats: POINT to row 1.
SAY: Birds are nice. But nice won't get a principal spending money.
POINT to row 3.
SAY: Skin cancer is serious. An expert backs it.
That's my strongest, so it goes last.
SAY: Each argument gets one proof.
A fact, an expert or a story. I used all three.
ASK: Why didn't I put skin protection first?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: so it builds; they remember the last
trap: three arguments that are really the same one.
Fix: ask is this a new reason or the same reason again?
notes.stretch: Find a second proof for the strongest argument.
notes.help: Start from the proof table on the Supported Worksheet.
notes.prep: Model: three different arguments, one proof each, ranked. Cancer Council shade figure: check current wording. Critical feature: strongest last.
notes.sources: Cancer Council Australia, shade and UV guidance (up to 75% reduction).

slides.title: What kind of proof?
slides.pivot: ask is there a number, a who, or a happening?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: how did you know?

items.text: A vet says dogs need a walk every day.
Ninety per cent of us walk past the bins.
My nan grew up with no plastic at all.
Scientists say Arctic ice is shrinking.
Yesterday a magpie got tangled in a bag.

say: One finger: fact or number. Two: expert. Three: story.
trap: calling every sentence with a number a story.
Fix: ask did something happen to someone?
notes.stretch: Say which would convince a principal most.
notes.help: Look for a number, a job title, or a happening.

options.text: Skin cancer, then cooler play, then birds.
Birds, then cooler play, then skin cancer.
Cooler play, then skin cancer, then birds.
options.misconception: the weakest is the last thing they hear

beats: SAY: Same three arguments. Three orders.
ASK: Which order builds best?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what will they remember?
Less -> read A then B aloud, ask which ends stronger, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. It climbs. They leave with the strongest.
trap: pointing to A because strongest first grabs attention.
Fix: say the opening grabs them; the last argument stays with them.
notes.prep: Decision point before ranking. Under 80% means one more ranking done together.

slides.title: Rank it
slides.pivot: find the strongest first, put it last, then order the rest
slides.followUp: cold call one board: why is that one strongest?

items.text: Longer lunch. A: more play. B: we eat properly. C: fewer fights.
items.answer: A, B, C or A, C, B (with a reason)

items.text: Class pet. A: pets are cute. B: we learn to care. C: pets calm worried kids.
Recycling bins. A: tidier yard. B: less landfill. C: bins look nice.

say: Write the three letters in order. Strongest last.
trap: ranking by which they like most, not which convinces.
Fix: ask which would make the principal say yes?
notes.stretch: Add a proof to the strongest.
notes.prep: Guided ranking. Accept a different order with a sound reason. SC2.

slides.title: Gather my proof
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by writing three arguments for your own speech, with proof, strongest last.

notes.answer: three different arguments, each with proof, strongest last
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Your three arguments and proof. Strongest goes last.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: is that a new reason? Where's your proof?
ASK: Read your strongest argument and proof to your partner.
30 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: a reason plus a fact, expert or story
trap: Fix: student adds one fact, expert or story to each.
notes.stretch: Extension: test proof for trust, then add a story.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a ranking done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent application to their own speech; S3 drafts the opening. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in the student's three ranked arguments with proof

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A speech asks for a vegie garden at school.
Reasons: A fresh lunches, B it looks nice, C we learn where food comes from. Rank them, strongest last.

notes.answer: B, A, C or B, C, A (B first)
beats: SAY: A new speech. Rank the reasons.
ASK: Write the three letters, strongest last, and why.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B first
RECORD who puts B last. Conference list for S3.
trap: B last because it is the easiest to see.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new speech. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Which proof in your speech will your audience remember most?

notes.answer: open - my story; my number; my expert
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that your strongest argument comes last?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Which proof in your speech will your audience remember most?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: my story; my number; my expert
notes.prep: Arguments go in the speech folder for S3. SC2.
